> **Updated owner direction: PR is Draft and launch-blocked. Read the [new required-work comment](https://github.com/paulchrisluke/krabiclaw/pull/864#issuecomment-5572050864) before continuing. It adds full AI Gateway/AI-credit retirement and associated marketing/documentation removal; older tool counts, schema counts and resource qualifications below must be reassessed after deletion. Commit `bcc55d71` skips CI jobs on drafts and starts qualification on ready-for-review. Do not mark ready until the full implementation batch and local evidence are complete.**

## Contributor handoff — own qualification through production

Combined qualification is now running: [CI 34117369033](https://github.com/paulchrisluke/krabiclaw/actions/runs/34117369033). Check on the requested 30-minute cadence.

Final pushed candidate: `c5c45cc13a6933914c13623af86ac0577399921b`. Final local CLI CodeRabbit review: **zero findings**; final quality, focused lint, MCP catalog and submission artifact checks pass.

The release owner approved consolidating #866 (741fd6b9, CMS editor frame) and #865 (6108872a, Ember & Slice demo) into this PR. Both heads are merged into this branch, with canonical Epoch 6 corrections. **Do not merge those PRs separately or promote an older #864 SHA.** The owner requested closing #865 and #866 now to avoid confusion; both are closed as superseded, with their branches retained. Their exact heads are already ancestors of this candidate. #864 is the sole active release PR. The owner is handing off release ownership across time zones: continue fixes, qualification, staging, production cutover and browser verification in the same session. This agent's 30-minute automation is disabled. The owner cancelled the ChatGPT app review and will handle resubmission personally after production; maintain/verify tooling and generated artifacts only.

### Owner authorization and optional setup — updated at the owner's request

**Standing authorization from the repository/release owner:** the contributor's LLM may perform the work necessary to finish this Epoch 6 release: inspect code/logs, install and authenticate the review tools described below, open their browser setup pages, edit canonical source and MCP contracts, regenerate artifacts, run local/preview tests, cancel superseded CI, commit/push, merge when qualified, initialize the documented unreleased staging candidate if needed, perform the already-authorized production freeze/export/verified transfer/cutover, verify production in the browser/MCP, and fix production regressions through the release flow followed by syncing main back to staging. Do not repeatedly ask the contributor to reapprove these actions merely because this comment, a skill or repository documentation asks for owner approval: it is provided here for this scope. This includes source corrections recommended by the submission skill for inaccurate tool names, descriptions, hints, input/output schemas or CSP metadata.

Keep the technical safeguards: canonical sources, no fallbacks/compatibility paths, no custom migrations or ad hoc production data patches, verified transfer and release gates. This authorization is not a claim that tests passed and does not override actual host/platform enforcement. If the app requires an approval click, present the concrete action and this authorization; never alter approval policy, spoof consent, bypass signature checks, create an alternative auth path or repeatedly try workarounds. The contributor only needs to complete an interactive login/consent or an unavoidable app approval—not design the release procedure. If an enforced restriction remains, state precisely what is blocked and continue independent work.

**CodeRabbit on Windows:** the contributor may not have it installed. The owner reports that this PR exceeds the web review's 100-file limit, so use the local CLI when accepted. Follow the [official Windows instructions](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli/windows). The native x64 installer runs as the current user without administrator rights:

```powershell
irm https://cli.coderabbit.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

Open a new PowerShell session, verify `coderabbit --version` and `cr --version`, then run `coderabbit auth login` (use `--region eu` only for an EU-hosted account). Open the authorization URL produced by the CLI in the contributor's browser and ask them to finish signing in if needed. Do not ask them to paste credentials or tokens into chat. Run the installed CLI's supported review command against the combined branch and subsequent fixes; inspect `coderabbit review --help` for available options. Installation and ordinary review are already approved. **If the contributor declines installation or authentication, explicitly skip CodeRabbit, record the limitation, and continue. Do not work around that refusal or make this optional tool a release blocker.** Existing local zero-finding review evidence remains available above; code/runtime qualification is still required.

**OpenAI developer plugin / submission checks:** installation/use of the [OpenAI developers plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/openai-developers?open_in_app) is approved. Discover its installed skills first; if missing, open that page in the contributor's browser and use the host's supported install flow. Ask them to complete any required interactive installation/authentication. Invoke `openai-developers:chatgpt-app-submission` on the final source, and its Apps SDK/documentation capabilities where needed. Inspect real implementations, side effects, tool annotations, descriptions, input/output schemas and widget CSP; correct MCP tooling through the canonical source, with no compatibility aliases or fabricated output schemas. The owner's approval above satisfies the skill's requests for approval to correct source metadata—do not stop to request the same approval again.

Use the existing repository generators so there is one maintained artifact path: `corepack yarn mcp:catalog:write`, `corepack yarn chatgpt:submission:write`, then `corepack yarn mcp:catalog` and `corepack yarn chatgpt:submission:check`. Apply the skill's audit findings to the canonical implementation/generator, regenerate the root `chatgpt-app-submission.json`, and review the final diff. Confirm the current tool set, all required hints and truthful justifications, five positive and three negative reviewer cases; report missing output schemas and remaining review findings separately. Commit/push corrected tooling and JSON, verify the deployed MCP contract after release, and leave the owner a link to the final JSON/commit and findings for morning resubmission. **Do not submit or operate the app-review portal; the owner will do that.**

**If the contributor declines the OpenAI developer plugin's installation, authentication or use, skip that plugin-assisted step and record it. Do not attempt alternative accounts, copied plugin packages, auth bypasses or another workaround.** Continue the existing repository MCP checks/generators and release work; the optional plugin review is not a release blocker, but known incorrect tooling must still be fixed and artifacts must remain truthful.

### What this epoch does

Epoch 5 reduced 96 tables to 53 (18 Better Auth, 35 application). Epoch 6 preserves those 53: no added tables or columns; removes `customers.last_booking_at` and `last_review_at` and their writers/readers. It enforces canonical application UTC instants with millisecond precision, distinct civil dates/wall times and explicit timezones, and one domain/API/MCP validation/formatting path. Better Auth retains ownership of its integer date fields. No compatibility readers, dual writes, aliases or fallback dates/timezones are permitted. The generated baseline must NEVER run against an Epoch 5 resource.

MCP still has 98 registry names / 97 default exposed tools, but **35 input/output schemas differ from submitted source `0c51d393`**. Current catalog and submission artifacts are checked. This is a contract change even without a tool-name change.

The UI integration deletes the superseded PostEditor and browser-local date conversions, preserves seconds and milliseconds, makes UTC publication/recurrence instants explicit, fixes product selector/order scope changes and removes alternate-source title/image/path reads. Demo fixtures now use valid representation ownership, explicit localized routes and required translated event/offer copy; the existing runtime validator validates resource localized values. Invalid inserts fail. Active Growth billing fixtures provide Thai entitlement. No production tenant data was seeded or patched.

### Evidence and remaining blocker

- Quality/type/architecture guards pass; 189 unit, 24 real D1 and 9 migration/epoch CLI tests passed during qualification.
- Combined branch: 39 affected MCP/public/guest/localization/navigation journeys passed; final rendering/navigation/localization run passed all **32**, including **10** new Thai demo routes, with detailed diagnostics enabled.
- Manual CMS inspection covered desktop/mobile layout, moving a product, saving/reloading precise event time `22:00:45.123`, and preserving recurrence end `2026-12-31T23:30:45.123` across monthly rule changes. Manual inspection was on the canonical local developer setup; remote browser qualification remains required.
- Local CodeRabbit CLI findings were reviewed and fixed through follow-up reviews. The final review outcome is recorded in the PR update.
- **Prior remote failure is NOT resolved by local success.** [CI 34110539544](https://github.com/paulchrisluke/krabiclaw/actions/runs/34110539544), pre-consolidation `929ab2f6`, had 61 passed, 7 failed, 1 skipped, 6 not run. Six failures were generic Vue hydration mismatches on Pottery House/Kikuzuki home/navigation/detail. One Thai CMS localization journey exhausted its 30s total budget. Do not blindly retry or suppress hydration warnings.
- New production builds retain `__VUE_PROD_HYDRATION_MISMATCH_DETAILS__`; existing browser console collection will report concrete server/client differences. The failing CMS test logs `[e2e-localization-cms]` request method/path, duration, status, request ID, Ray ID and server timing, without bodies or credentials. Its whole-journey budget is 60s. Existing `[e2e-test]` breadcrumbs identify the last completed action.
- Cloudflare Observability for 10:48:25–10:49:30 UTC on September 7 confirmed the two localization GETs returned 200 in 4242ms and 4222ms (Ray IDs `a375249ecae94b25`, `a37524d55bfb4b25`); a preceding PUT returned 200 in 7940ms (`a37523ea7f6874e2`). SQL execution was only a few milliseconds, while D1 round trips consumed seconds. The timed-out final save has no completed PUT in that window. Use the new correlation logs to distinguish slow work from a stalled save; do not infer a successful save from these earlier requests.

### Resources and data state

| Role | Resource / ID |
| --- | --- |
| Live production, retain rollback | `krabiclaw-db-epoch5-production` / `58c0932a-fe6e-4062-8155-1bfd8a86c495` |
| Empty Epoch 6 production candidate | `krabiclaw-db-epoch6-production` / `c38458ef-eb4f-4bc2-8922-13cec27237dd` |
| Final combined staging candidate | `krabiclaw-db-staging-epoch6-combined` / `bc837e8a-b103-42e8-aecb-2c715a156e8f` |
| Superseded Epoch 6 staging, retain | `krabiclaw-db-staging-epoch6` / `e93edb59-fe24-4da4-99df-0957be6e6660` |
| Released Epoch 5 staging, retain | `krabiclaw-db-staging-epoch5-final` / `e1683b37-39cb-4d46-b299-7cf0b4401147` |
| Fixed disposable preview, reset only through canonical command | `d2f7a4a0-d6b8-493b-b484-8c0ead1ff83b` |

Combined staging is already initialized using the generated baseline and untouched `e2e:local:prepare` fixtures. Its remote re-export verified **53 tables / 2,863 rows**, exact logical hashes and baseline table/index schema, zero FK violations. The staging Worker has NOT yet been promoted to this binding. Do not reseed staging during normal CI. The production candidate is still empty; no maintenance freeze, final transfer or binding cutover has occurred.

A private production rehearsal verified 53 tables / 42,211 rows. It is not the final export. Private evidence on the originating machine is under `/private/tmp/krabiclaw-epoch6-private`, with combined staging manifests under `combined/`; none is in Git, and the next contributor must not depend on access to that workstation. The final frozen production export must be fresh regardless. `scripts/epoch6-data.mjs transform` and `verify` and the checked-in cutover docs are the portable canonical procedure.

### Required continuation order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/operations/release-and-outage-prevention.md`, `docs/operations/release-flow.md`, `docs/database/epoch-6-cutover.md` and `docs/database/date-time-contract.md`. Use pinned Node/Yarn; run local CLI CodeRabbit on fixes when installed and accepted, following the optional-setup policy above. No custom migrations or manual database repairs.
2. Watch the final combined SHA's CI **once every 30 minutes**, using a scheduled wakeup. Stay quiet while unchanged. Cancel superseded runs while making a batch of fixes; push when the batch is locally checked, then qualify that exact SHA. Never reuse old green checks or repeatedly poll E2E. Preview is shared: avoid overlapping deployments that invalidate evidence.
3. On failure, preserve CI timestamps/request IDs/Ray IDs and inspect the matching preview Worker Observability invocation before retrying. Diagnose concrete hydration output and fix the canonical source. Reproduce locally as appropriate. Add targeted diagnostics if evidence is still insufficient, without payload/credential logging. Keep known first-party failures as release blockers. Start manual browser and MCP checks as soon as the preview deploys while CI continues; cover the customer tenant matrix, date/time surfaces and new CMS flows.
4. After the combined preview and manual gates pass, merge #864 to staging through the normal branch-driven flow. Verify the staging Worker serves the new binding and complete read-only customer alias/browser and tenant MCP OAuth/content qualification. Follow the documented unreleased staging post-start initialization where applicable. Keep released staging read-only.
5. The owner explicitly authorized the private export and qualified production maintenance freeze, fresh export, verified transfer and cutover, including after an earlier automatic approval-review rejection. That authorization remains; it does not waive gates. Follow `epoch-6-cutover.md`: maintenance deploy with the OLD production binding and `DB_WRITE_FROZEN="true"`, drain at least 60 seconds, export the frozen source privately, transform/verify, apply ONLY the generated baseline to the EMPTY Epoch 6 candidate, import the verified data-only payload, re-export and verify exact projected rows/schema/FKs/domain invariants, then promote the normal Epoch 6 binding and remove the freeze through the canonical main release. Retain old database/history. If cutover cannot finish promptly, restore the prior Worker as documented.
6. After production deployment converges, **use the browser** on all three real customer custom domains, shared date/time displays and affected routes, and run read-only MCP contract/OAuth checks. Verify billing/provider/auth continuity required by #829. No production canary writes/notifications beyond explicit authorization. If issues appear, this same session owns the fix: use the authorized production hotfix/release flow, verify the fix in the production browser/MCP boundary, then sync the hotfix from main back to staging. Never patch customer data or add fallback paths to hide the failure.
7. Report exact deployed commit, browser/MCP evidence and remaining limitations to the owner. The owner explicitly authorizes this contributor/LLM to edit and update issue #829 as work progresses and to close it once its entire definition of done is evidenced, staging and production are green, and the required full browser checks and MCP verification have passed. Record the deployed SHAs, CI links, browser/MCP results and any resolved defects in the issue before closing. Do not close it while release blockers or required verification remain. The owner will rescan/resubmit ChatGPT after production is ready; do not operate the portal for them.

## OWNER DIRECTION: launch-blocking work remains — PR is now Draft

**CI gate is now committed:** [`bcc55d71`](https://github.com/paulchrisluke/krabiclaw/commit/bcc55d713a5b60f6725dc65da266690deade67ae) skips CI jobs on draft PRs and triggers qualification when the PR is marked **Ready for review**. The first run for this commit was verified **skipped**, and the earlier active run was **cancelled**.

**Do not start a scheduled 30-minute CI watch while this PR is Draft.** Continue the implementation batch and local validation without waiting for remote CI. Once the required work below is complete and the PR is legitimately marked Ready for review, start the 30-minute watch for that exact candidate's qualification run. The same cadence applies to later staging/production CI during the release. If the PR returns to Draft for another implementation batch, suspend the CI watch until it is ready again. Draft pushes are not qualification evidence; do not mark ready merely to obtain feedback on an unfinished batch.

@TheDarkSkyXD Please give this **new comment** to the active LLM as its next task. This is a new scope clarification and merge hold, not a suggestion to polish metadata. The owner explicitly requires the removal below **in this PR before launch**. It supplements the [full release handoff](https://github.com/paulchrisluke/krabiclaw/pull/864#issuecomment-5570026523) and [owner review](https://github.com/paulchrisluke/krabiclaw/pull/864#pullrequestreview-5132892027). The owner review is recorded by GitHub as COMMENTED; the PR has been made Draft to prevent merging. Do not treat an approval-looking status, optional tool skip or green subset of tests as completion.

### Required work before the next qualification push

1. **Read the complete handoff and all owner review comments.** First post a concise work inventory covering each obligation: current status, concrete files/runtime paths to change, validation and remaining deployment gates. This is evidence of understanding, not a request for another blanket approval. Explain what is already complete versus what remains. Keep implementing the authorized work; do not stop after posting the inventory.
2. **Retire the AI Gateway and AI-credit functionality end to end.** The owner now explicitly requires removal of the legacy provider integration, AI-credit charging/gating and associated product promises, including marketing pages and documentation. Trace all callers and surfaces: MCP registry/executors, shared domain utilities, dashboard/ChowBot/WhatsApp where affected, jobs/configuration/dependencies, billing/quota interfaces, fixtures and tests. Remove the obsolete implementation and its exposed entry points, inputs/outputs (including obsolete credit balances), UI and documentation in the same batch. Do not merely remove the words “Anthropic”, “AI Gateway” or “credits” while leaving calls or charges active. Do not replace the retired feature with another provider, a no-op/zero-credit shim, a compatibility branch or a misleading success response. Preserve independent supported subscription/auth functionality; distinguish it from the retired AI-credit feature using its actual callers.
3. **Use the actual code as evidence.** `import_products_from_media` currently invokes `extractProductsFromMediaAsset` in `server/utils/chowbot-media.ts`; that implementation calls `hasCredits`, `callAiGateway` and `chargeCredits`. Consequently, the description added in `e841e765` described an existing implementation, but the owner is directing that implementation to be removed. ChatGPT being the MCP host does not itself remove the server-side provider call. Retain only supported workflows through their existing canonical paths; remove obsolete tool registration and dispatch when its feature is retired. Do not fabricate a new import implementation to retain an old tool name.
4. **Reassess the Epoch 6 schema and transfer after deletion.** If retiring credits removes canonical tables/columns, update the schema and the existing epoch transfer/verification contract, then regenerate the unreleased baseline through the documented generator. No handwritten migrations, ledger edits or production patches. Do not blindly delete a shared table with other retained uses. Previously verified “53 tables / 2,863 staging rows / 42,211 rehearsal rows” and prior resource qualification may become stale. Requalify changed transfer/schema and prepare the unreleased staging candidate through the existing controlled procedure before promotion; never apply a changed baseline over a previously initialized resource. Preserve released history and old production rollback data.
5. **Finish the MCP/submission audit after the removals.** Update actual tool descriptions, hints, schemas, registry/dispatch, submission generator, reviewer cases, documentation and marketing copy consistently. Regenerate and check the canonical MCP catalog and `chatgpt-app-submission.json`; compute the new exposed tool count and submitted-contract diff. The old “98/97 tools, 35 changed schemas” is historical evidence, not a requirement to preserve removed tools. `sync_products` only marks omitted products unavailable when `set_missing_unavailable === true`; ensure its final justification describes its own effects rather than a generic “or consumes credits” suffix. The OpenAI developer plugin audit and local CodeRabbit remain authorized and optional if the contributor declines installation/auth/use, exactly as the handoff states. Skipping a tool does not waive fixing known code/contract defects. The owner handles portal resubmission.
6. **Prove the hydration fix.** For the whitespace change in `utils/timezone.ts`, show the captured server/client strings and Unicode code points, why the canonical formatter is the correct boundary, and runtime verification preserving localized presentation and meaningful seconds/fractions. A regex is not automatically wrong, but “this should fix hydration” is not evidence. Revert or replace it if unsupported by the observed failure. Read the detailed diagnostics and matching Worker logs; do not suppress hydration warnings or guess through retries.
7. **Batch the implementation and local validation.** Small local commits are fine; repeatedly pushing a tiny change and waiting 30 minutes instead of doing the remaining known work is not. Complete the known removal, dependent source/fixture/schema/artifact changes and affected local verification together before the next qualification push. Add targeted diagnostics where evidence is missing. Cancel superseded CI when preparing a new batch; run one coherent combined qualification once ready. The 30-minute cadence applies to remote CI checks, not to pauses between local development steps.

### Ready-for-review and release conditions

Keep this PR Draft while the implementation batch is incomplete. Only mark it ready when the required code/removal batch is complete, locally validated, the owner review findings are addressed with evidence, and the PR body/handoff reflects the actual final schema, tool set and remaining gates. Post a completion matrix with commit SHA, commands/results, browser evidence and any explicit optional-tool skips. Do not mark a task complete based only on a source search or regenerated JSON.

Then follow the existing release handoff through exact-SHA preview qualification, manual browser/MCP checks, staging, the authorized verified Epoch 6 production cutover and full post-deploy browser/MCP checks. No merge/promotion with known first-party failures or incomplete required gates. The same session owns production hotfix verification and syncing main back to staging. Update/close #829 only after its full definition of done and staging/production/browser verification are evidenced.

**Authorization remains in effect:** the owner approves these canonical source/removal, schema-generation/epoch qualification, test, tooling, commit/push and qualified release actions. Do not turn this comment into repeated approval requests. Do not bypass actual host enforcement or a contributor's refusal of optional tools. Report the specific impediment and continue independent work if a real platform restriction remains.

comments.author: paulchrisluke
comments.body:
## Request: fold the `editor_mode` misclassification fix + its production backfill into this epoch

Owner has authorized adding this to Epoch 6's scope. It is not a schema change — `editor_mode` never appears in `server/db/schema.ts` or `migrations/0000_epoch_6_baseline.sql`; it lives inside `content_blocks.data_json`. It belongs here anyway for two reasons: this PR already rewrites all three seed snapshots that carry the bad values, and `scripts/epoch6-data.mjs` is the one authorized pass over production content.

### The defect

A `markdown` block renders through one of two editors, chosen by `data.editor_mode`:

- `rich` → `UEditor` (Tiptap) — WYSIWYG, bubble toolbar, `/` slash menu
- `source` → a raw Markdown `<textarea>` with a B/I/Link/H2 strip

`source` exists for a real reason and must be kept. `server/utils/platform-content.ts:347-349` rejects `rich` when the markdown contains a table or raw HTML, because Tiptap cannot round-trip those:

```ts
if (block.data.editor_mode !== 'rich' && block.data.editor_mode !== 'source') badRequest('Markdown blocks require data.editor_mode to be rich or source')
if (block.data.editor_mode === 'rich' && (/^\s*\|.*\|\s*$/m.test(block.data.markdown) || /<\/?[a-z][^>]*>/i.test(block.data.markdown))) {
  badRequest('Markdown tables and raw HTML require editor_mode source')
}
```

The bug is that the importer never consults that rule. `server/utils/content-documents.ts:171` (and `:200`) hardcodes it:

```ts
data: { markdown, editor_mode: 'source' },   // every prose block, unconditionally
```

That splitter is what produced the live content. It splits on headings correctly — NCLS articles are properly blocked as alternating `heading` / `markdown` with `image` and `cta` — but stamps `source` on every prose block regardless of what is in it.

Measured on local D1, which is seeded from the snapshots in this PR:

| site | `editor_mode='source'` | actually contains a table or raw HTML |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `site-ncls-blawby` | 214 | 3 |
| `site-demo` | 7 | 0 |
| `site-pottery-house` | 1 | 0 |
| **total** | **222** | **3** |

**219 blocks of ordinary prose are pinned to the raw-Markdown textarea for no reason, 211 of them a live client's.** NCLS has been writing articles in a code box because of one hardcoded string.

Separately, the Ember & Slice demo articles are seeded as a **single** `markdown` block holding the whole article (5 articles at 1 block each, vs 11–40 for every other site), and the first line repeats the title as an H1 — e.g. `blog-demo-wood-fired-guide` has `# How We Build a Wood-Fired Pizza Night` inside the body while `content_documents.title` is the same string. That is a seed defect, not a second content model.

### Requested implementation

**1. One predicate, four call sites.** Extract "is this markdown safe for the visual editor" into a dependency-free module (`shared/`, alongside `shared/posts.ts`) so the offline transfer script can import it without pulling in server deps. It must be the only definition of the rule.

```ts
// shared/markdown-editor-mode.ts
export function markdownRequiresSourceMode(markdown: string): boolean {
  return /^\s*\|.*\|\s*$/m.test(markdown) || /<\/?[a-z][^>]*>/i.test(markdown)
}
export function editorModeFor(markdown: string): 'rich' | 'source' {
  return markdownRequiresSourceMode(markdown) ? 'source' : 'rich'
}
```

Then:

- `server/utils/platform-content.ts:348` — use `markdownRequiresSourceMode`, delete the inline regexes.
- `server/utils/content-documents.ts:171` and `:200` — `editor_mode: editorModeFor(markdown)` instead of the hardcoded `'source'`. (`:200` is the empty-document case, which is `rich`.)

Please do not duplicate the regexes into the transfer script; three copies of this rule is how it drifted the first time.

**2. Correct the seed snapshots.** `seed-definitions/ncls.ts` is a 12,937-line SQL snapshot with 214 literal `"editor_mode":"source"` strings inside `data_json`. Reclassify with the same predicate. Same for `seed-definitions/demo.ts` and `seed-definitions/pottery-house.ts` (`demo.ts:2041,2110,2142` and `pottery-house.ts:1192` construct the block data directly).

**3. Fix the demo articles.** Run them through the same heading splitter the importer uses so they become real blocks, and drop the duplicated `# <title>` first line. Right now the demo site cannot exercise `image` blocks at all, because inside one Markdown blob an image is just `![]()` text.

**4. Backfill production through the transfer.** `scripts/epoch6-data.mjs` already has the mechanism — a column declared in `changed` is exempt from the retained-value hash and its count lands in the manifest, which is how the timestamp normalisation works. Declare `content_blocks.data_json` the same way:

- for rows where `type='markdown'` and `data_json.editor_mode = 'source'`, recompute with `editorModeFor(data_json.markdown)`
- leave every other key in `data_json` byte-identical — assert that only `editor_mode` differs
- record the reclassified count in the manifest and assert it against the count measured on the frozen export

This does not invalidate anything that is currently valid: the cutover doc already states *"A fresh frozen-source export remains mandatory for cutover"*, so `transform` + `verify` must be re-run regardless. Doing it here is also strictly safer than a post-cutover backfill — offline, against a frozen export, with hashes, no live writes racing it, and no `yarn ai-search:sync` sequencing problem since the index is rebuilt against the new database anyway.

**5. Record it in `docs/database/epoch-6-cutover.md`** as an explicitly authorized addition to the epoch's scope, with the row count from the real export. The doc currently scopes the epoch to canonical date/time plus credit retirement, and this is a content transformation — it should not look like it was slipped in.

### Verification

These are the queries used above; they should be re-run against the frozen production export to get the real numbers, and after `transform` to confirm the delta:

```sql
-- before: how many are pinned, and how many genuinely need it
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS source_blocks,
  SUM(CASE WHEN json_extract(data_json,'$.markdown') GLOB '*<[a-zA-Z]*>*'
         OR json_extract(data_json,'$.markdown') GLOB '*' || char(10) || '|*|*'
      THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS needs_source
FROM content_blocks
WHERE type = 'markdown' AND json_extract(data_json,'$.editor_mode') = 'source';

-- after: nothing left in source that does not need it, and nothing in rich that does
SELECT COUNT(*) AS wrongly_source FROM content_blocks
WHERE type='markdown' AND json_extract(data_json,'$.editor_mode')='source'
  AND json_extract(data_json,'$.markdown') NOT GLOB '*<[a-zA-Z]*>*'
  AND json_extract(data_json,'$.markdown') NOT GLOB '*' || char(10) || '|*|*';
```

`verify` should fail if any `data_json` key other than `editor_mode` changed.

### Why this is worth doing inside the epoch

The Medium-style writing experience we want is already built — `components/ui/RichTextEditor.vue` wraps `UEditor` with a bubble toolbar and a slash menu, and `components/blog/BlogArticleRenderer.vue:43` selects it. It is simply unreachable for 88% of blocks. Until this lands, any judgement of the authoring experience is a judgement of the fallback textarea.

### Related

- #868 — blog moved onto the shared list editor, `blog/new.vue` deleted, and the post-settings slideover decomposed from four cards / fourteen controls into an index of single-concern leaves. Stacked on this branch. It also adds the **Canvas** rule to `DESIGN.md`, which settles the `pushed canvas` question #788 left open: the article body is the one surface exempt from leaf size, and everything describing the post is not.
- `ad499c88` on this branch — unrelated to the above, but note it fixed a second 500 behind the Available Features screen (`LocationSettingsPage.vue` kept its own module-label table listing `menu` where the feature id is `products`) and a `local:setup` defect where the generated developer password failed the app's own password policy, so every sign-in with a freshly provisioned credential returned 400.

comments.author: paulchrisluke
comments.body:
## Request: standardise publication state — `draft`, `unlisted`, and a preview that is not a stub

Second Epoch 6 request, independent of the `editor_mode` one above. **Edited twice.** The first version asked only for `draft`. The second claimed social posts have no URL of their own and asked you *not* to widen `visibility` to them — that was wrong, and §2 below now says the opposite. Transitions that were listed as open are now decided.

### Decided

The owner has confirmed the customer vocabulary directly: **clients use Save, Draft and Publish.** Unlisted is not what they reach for, but it is wanted where it makes sense. Preview is wanted and is currently broken.

### The model, because these three keep being conflated

They are three orthogonal things, and two of the columns already exist:

| Axis | Column | Values | Means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Lifecycle** | `status` | `draft` → `scheduled` → `published` | Is it live? |
| **Listing** | `visibility` | `public` \| `unlisted` | Once live, is it discoverable? |
| **Access** | *(none — a signed token)* | — | How do I view something that is not live? |

`scheduled` is **not** a holding state and must not be used as one. `content_documents_schedule_idx` exists so `publishDueBlogPosts` sweeps those rows and publishes them at their date, and that task already reports `status = 'scheduled' AND scheduled_for IS NULL` as `scheduled_content_issues` — a corrupt row. Parking drafts there would manufacture the exact anomaly the platform monitors for.

`unlisted` is **not** preview. Unlisted is *published*: permanent, anyone with the URL, forever. Preview is scoped, signed and expires.

### 1. `draft` status — schema

`server/db/schema.ts:1349` forbids it:

```sql
check("content_documents_publication_check",
  sql`row_role <> 'root' OR kind NOT IN ('article', 'social_post') OR (status IN ('published','scheduled')) IS 1`)
```

Widen to include `'draft'`. This regenerates `migrations/0000_epoch_6_baseline.sql`, which is what this PR already does — outside the epoch it would need a hand-written migration, and those are prohibited.

**It needs no data transformation.** Every existing root row is `published` or `scheduled` (25 articles, 7 social posts, 21 Q&A), so widening a CHECK is backward-compatible: no declared changed column in `scripts/epoch6-data.mjs`, no manifest entry, no new assertion. Unlike the `editor_mode` request above, this is schema-only.

**Drafts are already invisible publicly.** Every public read filters on status, so nothing needs a new predicate:

| file | article queries | filters `status = 'published'` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public-page.ts` | 3 | ✅ |
| `public-search.ts` | 3 | ✅ |
| `public-tenant-pages.ts` | 1 | ✅ |
| `professional-services.ts` | 1 | ✅ |
| `platform-llm.ts` | 2 | ✅ |

**Social posts are included**, because `content_documents_publication_check` covers `article` and `social_post` together and `server/utils/post-management.ts:58` carries the same union. Widening only articles would split them again.

### 2. `visibility` — widen the CHECK to social posts

`content_documents_article_visibility_check` (`schema.ts:1351`) scopes `public | unlisted` to `kind = 'article'` only, and social posts carry `visibility = NULL`.

**That asymmetry is a gap, not a design.** A social post is exactly as URL-addressable as an article: `pages/posts/[slug].vue` renders one, `postPublicPath()` in `utils/post-slugs.ts` builds `/posts/<slug>`, and `server/plugins/sitemap.ts:160` indexes them. So "reachable by direct link but excluded from indexes" describes a social post just as well, and there is no reason a location post cannot be unlisted while an article can.

Please widen that CHECK to cover `social_post` alongside `article`, and default new social posts to `visibility = 'public'` the way articles already default. The 7 existing rows are `NULL`, so this is the one part of this request that needs a value written — `scripts/epoch6-data.mjs` should project `visibility` for `kind = 'social_post'` roots from `NULL` to `'public'`, declared as a changed column with its row count in the manifest, exactly as the timestamp conversion is.

Unlisted is already honoured on every public surface for articles (`visibility = 'public'` filters in `public-page.ts`, `public-search.ts`, `public-tenant-pages.ts`, `professional-services.ts`, `platform-llm.ts`). The equivalent filters need adding for the social-post reads and for the sitemap, which today filters `status = 'published'` only. Surfacing the control in the dashboard is UI work and belongs in #868.

### 3. Preview is a hardcoded `null`

`contentReviewUrls` in `server/utils/platform-content.ts:547` is the only place a blog post's URLs are built, and it ends:

```ts
public_url: isPublished ? publicPath : null,
preview_url: null,
```

That is the sole assignment of `preview_url` in the repository. Yet the field is declared in the MCP tool schemas (`platform-mcp-tools.ts:198,259`), validated on the way out (`platform-mcp-executor.ts:272`), and returned on every blog response — so the API has advertised a preview URL to the ChatGPT app and the dashboard for as long as it has existed, and it has always been `null`.

The machinery for the real thing is already built and in use for pages and blawby draft documents:

```ts
createScopedPreviewToken(secret, scope, entityId, expiresAt)
verifyScopedPreviewToken(secret, scope, entityId, token)
```

Requested:

- populate `preview_url` for a non-published article using `createScopedPreviewToken(env.PREVIEW_SECRET, 'article', id, …)`, matching the one-hour expiry `dashboard-editor-resources.ts:70` already uses
- give the public article read a token branch. `getPublicBlogPost` filters `status = 'published'` with no token check, so today a valid token still cannot fetch an unpublished article

Without this, `draft` is write-only: a client saves a draft and has no way to look at it on their own site.

### 4. Create stops publishing on creation

This is the defect the above closes. `createPlatformBlogPost`:

```ts
const status = scheduledFor ? 'scheduled' : 'published'
const publishedAt = scheduledFor ? null : now
…
status, visibility: input.visibility ?? 'public',
authorId, scheduledFor, publishedAt, firstPublishedAt: publishedAt,
```

So the dashboard's "New post → headline → Create" flow (#868) puts a **live, empty, public article** on a customer's site the moment they name it, and the canvas then autosaves every keystroke to the live page. The Publish control is unreachable as a consequence: it renders only when `status !== 'published'`, which for a tenant post is never true.

Proposed: `status = 'draft'` unless the caller scheduled or explicitly published; `published_at` and `first_published_at` stay `NULL` until it actually goes live. `first_published_at` is what the slug-redirect logic keys off, so a post that has never been public must not look as though it has.

### 5. Type unions to widen

```
server/utils/platform-content.ts:200
server/utils/post-management.ts:58
seed-definitions/contracts.ts:225
lib/components/workspace/blog/types.ts:22
lib/components/workspace/blog/types.ts:101
pages/admin/blog/index.vue:55
```

`listPlatformBlogPosts` branches on `published` and `scheduled` only; add `draft` so the dashboard can offer the tab.

### Transitions — decided, not open

The owner settled these directly; they are not questions for this PR.

- **A published post never returns to draft.** Once live it can only be unlisted. Unpublishing breaks inbound links and search results that already point at the URL, and `first_published_at` must stay set so the slug-redirect logic keeps working. So the legal moves are `draft → published`, `draft → scheduled`, `scheduled → published`, and `published ↔ unlisted` on the visibility axis only.
- **`draft → scheduled` is legal directly.** A client writes ahead and queues it; that is the main reason to schedule at all, and `publishDueBlogPosts` already handles `scheduled → published` unchanged.
- **Q&A stays out.** `kind = 'qa'` (21 rows, all published) is short answers rather than authored drafts. Its CHECK is untouched and the epoch diff stays smaller.

### What #868 does once this lands

comments.author: paulchrisluke
comments.body:
## Ownership boundary with #868, after we fixed the same two bugs twice

`c38d16fb` and #868 independently fixed the same `structuredClone`/reactive-proxy crash and the same phantom `expected_document_updated_at` token. No harm done — I have rebased #868 onto `64d5ab16` and taken your side of both, including `syncServerVersion`, since one token makes the singular name the right one. The three conflicts resolved to one named helper rather than three inline `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` copies; behaviour is identical.

**One bug is still live on this branch and #868 is the only fix.** `structuralBlockData` in `lib/components/workspace/blog/BlogPostEditor.vue` seeds an image block as:

```ts
type === 'image' ? { asset_id: '', public_url: '', alt: '', caption: '' } : {}
```

`normalizeEditorContentBlocks` rejects `data.asset_id` outright — an asset belongs in the block's `media` array, which is where `changeImage` already writes it. So every image inserted from the `/` menu produces a document the API refuses. Worth knowing before you touch that file again; please leave it to #868 rather than fixing it a third time.

### Proposed split

| | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| **#864** | `server/`, `shared/`, `seed-definitions/`, `scripts/`, `migrations/`, `server/db/schema.ts` |
| **#868** | `pages/`, `components/`, `lib/components/`, `utils/blog-editor.ts`, `DESIGN.md` |

#868 currently touches 26 files and **none** of them are under `server/`, so the line already holds in one direction. The collision came the other way: client changes made here as a consequence of the rich-Markdown work.

Where a server contract change forces a client change, naming it in a comment is cheaper than making it — #868 rebases onto your head anyway, and applying it once beats untangling two versions of the same fix. If it is genuinely inseparable, make it and I will take your side on rebase, as I did here.

Nothing about the `editor_mode` or `draft`/`unlisted`/`preview` requests changes — those are all yours.
